title: Vibe-Appliance per-app manifest
description: Schema for .appliance/manifest.json shipped by each Vibe app. See docs/MANIFEST_SCHEMA.md.

allOf._doc: Everything the appliance itself installs must still carry the full field set. `runtime` defaults to "appliance", and an ABSENT property satisfies a `properties` subschema, so every manifest written before this field existed matches this branch and validates exactly as it did before. A Sentinel module opts out by declaring runtime:"sentinel" - it has no subdomain (Falco and CrowdSec have no web surface), may have no image at all (the `ai` module ships no container), and publishes through its own ingress.

_doc.description: Free-form documentation/provenance note. Ignored by the renderer; useful for tagging where the manifest was imported from or recording divergence from upstream.

runtime.description: Which orchestrator installs and owns this unit. `appliance` (the default, and what every manifest written before this field existed means) is installed by lib/enable-app.sh into the `vibe` compose project on vibe_net. `sentinel` is installed by vibe-sentinel-installer into its own `vibe-sentinel` compose project, with its own Postgres, Redis and ingress; the appliance reads the manifest so the console can present one catalog, but renders NOTHING for it - no Caddy vhost, no path handler, no emergency frontend, no tunnel ingress. See docs/MANIFEST_SCHEMA.md#runtime.

sameProductAs.description: Slug of another catalog unit that is the SAME product shipped by a different installer - vibe-printer and sentinel-print both run ghcr.io/kisaesdevlab/vibe-printer, one packaging of one gateway. Symmetric by contract: each twin names the other, and the pair must span different runtimes (a same-runtime twin is just a duplicate manifest; tests/manifests/validate-manifests.test.js enforces both). The console renders an 'enable one, not both' note on each card and asks for confirmation before enabling the second copy.

extras.description: Additional GHCR image refs that ship with this app as a versioned set. Used by apps that need MORE than the server+client pair (e.g. vibe-shield ships engine + gateway + admin, all rolling forward together). update.sh re-tags every image listed here for the rollback path; without this, an app's auxiliary containers would silently stay on the new digest when a rollback fires against server/client only. Apps with only server+client omit this entirely.

subdomain.description: DNS label prepended to the appliance domain. May start with a digit (RFC 1123) so apps like vibe-1099 can use `1099` as their subdomain.

pathPrefix.description: Optional URL path segment, e.g. `time` serves the app at https://<host>/time/. Defaults to the slug with a leading `vibe-` stripped (vibe-tb -> /tb/). Set this when the product name and the slug diverge: the slug is the INTERNAL identifier (state.json keys, /opt/vibe/env/<slug>.env, container names, the per-app Postgres database) so renaming it is a data migration, whereas the URL is presentation and should be free to change. Must be unique across enabled apps — two sharing a prefix would collide in Caddy.

subdomains.description: Phase 8.5 v1.2 — opt-in multi-subdomain manifest. When present, this list controls EMERGENCY-ACCESS wiring only (HAProxy emits one frontend per item with emergencyPort). The PRIMARY Caddy vhost still uses the top-level `subdomain` field — per-subdomain Caddy routing is a future enhancement gated on backend container splits in the upstream Vibe-* repos. Vibe-Connect's staff/client split is the canonical use case. Manifests should declare BOTH the legacy `subdomain` field (for Caddy) AND `subdomains[]` (for HAProxy multi-port emergency access); declaring `subdomains` alone is allowed but means no Caddy vhost. The `emergencyPort` values across items must be unique per manifest (HAProxy refuses to bind the same port twice).

name.description: DNS label segment to prepend to the appliance domain. May start with a digit (RFC 1123). Dots allowed so a manifest can declare a multi-label subdomain (e.g. `gateway.shield` → `gateway.shield.<domain>`).

audience.description: Free-form label shown in the Emergency Access panel. Conventional values: 'staff', 'client', 'default'.

target.description: Caddy reverse-proxy target for this secondary subdomain (e.g. `vibe-connect-client:8080`). Consumed by lib/render-caddyfile.sh's render_extra_subdomain_vhosts; falls back to the manifest's routing.default_upstream when absent.

internal.description: When true, this subdomain is server-to-server only — lib/render-caddyfile.sh emits NO Caddy vhost for it and infra/cloudflared-up.sh adds NO tunnel ingress rule. Cross-app callers reach the service by container DNS over vibe_net (e.g. http://vibe-shield-gateway:8080). Used by apps that mix one PUBLIC surface (the primary subdomain → admin UI) with one or more INTERNAL ones (Vibe-Shield's `gateway.shield` Anthropic-shaped API). Applies independently to the primary subdomain entry too — setting `internal: true` on the entry whose `name` matches the manifest's top-level `subdomain` skips its path handler on the single-host vhost, equivalent to the old `userFacing: false` wholesale block. The emergencyPort frontend still emits regardless (UFW already gates emergency ports to LAN/Tailscale).

emergencyPort.description: TCP port on the emergency HAProxy proxy (Phase 8.5 Workstream D). Plain HTTP, UFW-gated to RFC1918 + Tailscale CGNAT. Maps to this app's routing.default_upstream. See docs/addenda/emergency-access.md §3 for the canonical port assignments. The emergency proxy is intrinsically staff-only via UFW; userFacing=false apps with a staff-admin UI (e.g. vibe-shield) MAY declare an emergencyPort so staff retain fallback access when Caddy or TLS is broken. Only truly headless server-to-server services (e.g. vibe-glm-ocr) should omit it entirely.

emergencyNote.description: Optional caveat displayed verbatim in CREDENTIALS.txt and the admin Emergency Access panel — e.g. for Vibe-Connect's client portal: 'Staff emergency access only. Client magic-link flows require HTTPS.'

userFacing.description: If false, the app is internal-only (consumed by other Vibe apps, never directly by users). Internal apps do not get an emergency port and may be excluded from the public landing page.

landingOrder.description: Optional sort key for the public landing page. Cards (app cards + operator-curated customCards) are rendered in ascending order; ties fall back to displayName for apps and insertion order for customCards. Omit for default behavior (treated as +Infinity, i.e. sorted to the end among manifest apps). Lets the operator pin high-traffic client surfaces (e.g. intake, portal sign-in) to the top of the grid.

clientLanding.description: Optional client-facing entry points surfaced as buttons on the public landing page at /. Each entry produces one button on the app's card under the standard path-prefix base URL (e.g. https://vibe.firm.com/tb<path>, where the prefix is the slug with the redundant `vibe-` stripped). Omit for the default single 'Open' button behavior. Skip entries that require per-client tokens (those are emailed by staff, not surfaceable on a static page).

order.description: Optional sort key for buttons WITHIN this card. Ascending; missing = sorted to end. Lets a manifest declare multiple entries while letting the operator decide which surfaces should appear first to clients.

hostPorts.description: Ports this unit publishes on the HOST. Appliance apps never set this - only Caddy and the emergency proxy publish, which is the appliance's own anti-pattern rule. It exists because a Sentinel module cannot avoid it: Wazuh agents dial 1514/1515, printers speak IPP on 631, and an MFP scanning to a share needs 445 - none of those can be reverse-proxied. Declaring them here is what lets EITHER installer detect a conflict on a shared host before a container fails to bind, which is how the appliance's Caddy on 0.0.0.0:443 and Vaultwarden on <mesh-ip>:443 currently collide with nothing to catch it.

portEnd.description: Inclusive end of a contiguous range (FTPS passive ports are the case). Omit for a single port.

bind.description: Which interface the publish is scoped to. `mesh` = the private-network IP only, `loopback` = 127.0.0.1 only, `lan` = an RFC1918 address, `any` = 0.0.0.0. Conflict detection treats `any` as colliding with everything on that port.

optional.description: True when the publish only happens behind an opt-in (NetBird's relay on 3478/udp). Conflict checks report it, but its absence is not a failure.

root_redirect.description: Path to 308-redirect the bare `/` to, for an app that serves nothing at its own root. Emitted only on ROOT-SERVED surfaces — the per-app Caddy vhost (subdomain-per-app mode, and rootServedOnly apps in single-host mode) and the app's emergency-proxy frontend — because those are the only places the appliance sends an operator to a bare `/`. Path-mounted apps are unaffected: their prefix handler already lands inside the app. Vibe-Printer is the motivating case: its API is at /v1 and its admin SPA is mounted at /admin, so `/` is a bare 404 and every URL the console advertises for it would be broken. Prefer fixing the app to serve something useful at its root; this exists so an app that cannot is still openable.

deny_paths.description: Paths Caddy answers with 404 instead of proxying, emitted ahead of every other handler for this app. For endpoints an app serves that are fine on vibe_net and on the UFW-gated emergency port but should not be world-readable once the app is fronted by Caddy — vibe-ai-router's unauthenticated /metrics (per-task-class request counts, provider names, breaker state) is the motivating case. NOT an authorization mechanism: it only closes the public edge, so anything reachable from inside vibe_net stays reachable there.

ownsInfra.description: Infrastructure this unit brings its OWN copy of, rather than using the appliance's shared instance. The appliance's standing rule is that nothing duplicates Postgres or Redis; this field is how a unit states that the rule does not apply to it and why. Sentinel's `core` owns all five: its Postgres carries the authentik and vaultwarden schemas (Vaultwarden migrates one-way over the firm's entire credential set, so sharing an instance is not a decision to make casually), and it runs its own cloudflared, Authentik and restic. Anything listed here is skipped by db-bootstrap and by the shared-URL env renderers.

optionalDepends.description: Other Vibe app slugs this app benefits from when enabled (e.g. vibe-tx-converter calls vibe-glm-ocr for OCR if available). Informational only — the appliance does NOT enforce these at enable time; an app whose optional dep is disabled will see its dependent features fail at runtime with whatever upstream error path the app itself produces. Consider wiring a preflight WARN in a future iteration.

requiredApps.description: Other Vibe app slugs that MUST already be enabled and healthy before this app can be enabled. Unlike optionalDepends this IS enforced: lib/enable-app.sh's pre-flight refuses the enable and names the missing app, rather than letting the operator discover it as a container that boots and immediately exits. Use only for a hard runtime dependency the app itself treats as fatal — Vibe-1040 is the case this exists for: its env schema requires a VIBE_AI_TOKEN, which only exists once vibe-ai-router is up to mint one, so without the router even the migration step fails.

bootOrder.description: Ascending start order within one runtime, for a stack whose units must come up in sequence with a health gate between each. `requiredApps` already expresses the hard edges (everything depends on Sentinel's `core`); this expresses the ordering WITHIN a tier that has no dependency edge to hang it on - Wazuh's indexer, manager and dashboard refuse mixed states and must move in that order. Appliance apps omit it: they are independent by design and any subset is a valid stack.

redis.description: Logical Redis DB index (0-15). Each app gets its own to prevent key collisions on the shared Redis instance.

dataOwner.description: Explicit uid:gid that /opt/vibe/data/apps/<slug>/ must be owned by, overriding the uid lib/enable-app.sh would otherwise read from the server image's USER directive. Needed when an app's containers do NOT all run as the same user but DO share one bind-mounted data directory — Vibe-1040 is the case: its Node api/worker and its Python sidecar come from different base images with different baked-in uids, and both read and write the encrypted blob store. The overlay pins every one of those services to this same uid:gid with a compose `user:` key; declaring it here is what keeps the host-side chown in agreement with that pin. Omit whenever the image-derived uid is correct, which is every other app.

requiredExtensions.description: Postgres extensions the app's migrations CREATE EXTENSION on first boot (e.g. ['vector','pg_search']). enable-app's pre-flight queries pg_available_extensions and refuses to start the app if any are missing — turning a confusing mid-migration failure into a clean preflight FAIL with a hint pointing at docker-compose.yml's postgres image.

passwordEnvKey.description: Name of an env-file key whose VALUE is the password the operator pastes into the app's login form. When set, the console reads /opt/vibe/env/<slug>.env at request time and surfaces that key's value as `password` on /api/v1/first-login. Used for credentials that the appliance GENERATES on enable (e.g. vibe-shield's GATEWAY_ADMIN_KEY) rather than bakes into the manifest. Takes precedence over the static `password` field if both are set.

note.description: Operator-facing note rendered in the admin First-login info card. Use for caveats like 'wizard at /install — may 404 on older images'.

health.description: How readiness is decided. A PATH (the appliance convention) is probed over HTTP and must return 200 only when the unit is fully ready - DB migrated, dependencies up. A SCRIPT is run instead, exit 0 meaning healthy; Sentinel modules use this because several of them have no HTTP surface to probe at all, and because a probe of Uptime Kuma has to assert the pinned build is the one running, not merely that something answered.

script.description: Path relative to the unit's own directory in its installer checkout, e.g. `healthcheck.sh`.

health_timeout_s.description: How long to wait for the app's /health endpoint to respond 200 during enable / update before declaring failure. Default 120. Apps that load large models (e.g. Vibe-GLM-OCR's vision model) may need 300+.

health_extra.description: Additional containers to health-check on enable and in doctor.sh, beyond the routing-derived one. `health` alone probes routing.matchers[0].upstream (or default_upstream), which is the surface Caddy fronts — an app whose other tier is never proxied (vibe-ai-router's /v1 gateway) would otherwise be reported healthy while that tier is down. Each entry must name a container the app's own overlay declares.

rootServedOnly.description: Set true when the app's web bundle requests assets from absolute root paths and its image has no base-path switch (no /docker-entrypoint.d/40-base-path.sh, no VITE_BASE_PATH). Such an app CANNOT be mounted at /<prefix>/: the shell loads and every asset request resolves against the host root — the appliance console — so the operator gets a blank page with a 200. The renderer then emits no path handler for it in any mode and gives it a root-served vhost at its own subdomain in domain mode, in BOTH routing modes. LAN/Tailscale has no per-app hostname to offer, so its emergency port becomes the access path and the console advertises that instead. Prefer fixing the app: adding base-path support upstream lets it path-mount like every other Vibe app and this flag can be dropped.

ingress.description: DESCRIBES where this unit is published, for a runtime that owns its own ingress. The appliance never renders from this - it is what lets the console link to a Sentinel module correctly without the appliance having to learn Cloudflare Access policies, gRPC http2Origin, WAF rate limits and ACME DNS-01 wildcards, all of which Sentinel's ingress already implements. Appliance apps omit it; their ingress comes from `routing`, `subdomain` and `rootServedOnly`.

access.description: Cloudflare Access posture. `bypass` is for machine-facing endpoints that cannot complete an interactive login - NetBird's agent traffic, and the Bitwarden clients that talk to Vaultwarden.

origin.description: http2 means an h2c origin (`http2Origin` in the tunnel config), which NetBird's gRPC requires and without which it does not work at all.

hostname.description: Host label under the firm domain, e.g. `wazuh`. Mesh-only names resolve to a private mesh IP in public DNS, which is allowed and is how the wildcard certificate covers them without a private CA.

resources.description: Floor this unit needs, checked as FREE capacity rather than installed capacity. The console runs it as a pre-flight before the Enable button is live: the appliance's reference host is a 1vcpu/2GB droplet and Sentinel's core alone wants 4 cores and 8 GB, so on most firm hosts the honest answer is a second host, and saying so up front beats a failed install.

diskFormula.description: Human-readable derivation for units whose disk need is not a constant, e.g. agent count x retention with headroom.

hostPrereqs.description: Host-level facts that must hold before this unit can run, expressed as data so both installers and doctor.sh check the same list. Every entry here is a real failure that is otherwise discovered late and cryptically: OpenSearch simply will not start below the vm.max_map_count floor, and Falco's modern eBPF probe needs a kernel with BTF or it silently falls back to privileged mode.

license.description: Surfaced in the console catalog so an operator sees the terms before installing. NEVER enforced - the appliance does not gate installs on an entitlement check, and gating a security and compliance tool behind a network call is the wrong trade.

seed.description: Optional. Run-once command (executed via docker exec on the server container) for apps whose admin-user seed is separate from migrations. enable-app.sh runs this after _wait_for_app_health succeeds and gates re-runs via state.apps.<slug>.seeded. See docs/MANIFEST_SCHEMA.md#seed.

harnessGate.description: Marks this unit as one whose upgrade is gated on a detection/integration harness having been run against the target version. The console SURFACES the state; the gate itself stays in vibe-sentinel-installer's upgrade.sh, where it was designed and tested and where there is deliberately no --force. These five families are gated because a break in them does not look like an outage: Uptime Kuma's socket.io API is unversioned, Vaultwarden migrates one-way over the firm's whole vault, NetBird is every agent's only path home, Authentik is the IdP, and Wazuh IS the detection engine - a broken decoder set reads as 'quiet'.

family.description: Key into the installer's versions/manifest.json images map.

disableRequires.description: Turning this unit off leaves a hole something else must fill, and the console must collect what that something is before proceeding. Set on Sentinel's Security Six modules (mesh, keys, pulse, print): a firm may legitimately use Tailscale instead of NetBird or 1Password instead of Vaultwarden, but the compliance scorecard still needs an answer, so 'off' without a recorded reason is refused rather than silently accepted.

preUninstallExport.description: Data export that MUST run before teardown. Incident records, reports, attestations and evidence are the firm's compliance artifacts, retained indefinitely, and several of them have to outlive the tool that produced them by years - so removal exports first and takes a typed confirmation to skip.

from.description: Source for the value. See docs/MANIFEST_SCHEMA.md. Note: this field is descriptive metadata — _render_app_env does literal @MARKER@ substitution against the env template, not lookup against this list.

uiBlock.description: Admin Settings page surface for this env var. Phase 8.5 Workstream C. Absence means tier 3 (not surfaced). See docs/addenda/admin-config-surface.md §3.

tier.description: 1 = inline-editable form field; 2 = read-only with copy-paste rotation hint; 3 = not surfaced (default).

category.description: Settings page tab. Required for tier 1.

input.description: Form input widget. Required for tier 1.

dynamic.description: If set, the client merges live values from a server-provided source into the static options list at render time. Currently only 'anthropic-models' is supported (GET /api/v1/admin/anthropic-models).

appliance.description: Where the value lives. shared = appliance.env (cascades to all apps); per-app = vibe-<slug>.env (default); both = declared at both levels with per-app override.

restartRequired.description: If true (default), saving this setting restarts dependent apps with rollback-on-health-failure. If false, send SIGHUP only (forward-compat — no Vibe app supports SIGHUP reload yet).

validate.description: Server-side validator name. Constrained to the dispatcher's known set so a typo (e.g. 'anthropic-key') fails schema validation rather than blowing up at save time.

testEndpoint.description: Console route the Test button POSTs current form values to (without persisting). See addendum §5.

dependsOnFields.description: Field names this field depends on, used for client-side conditional rendering.

showIf.description: Predicate keyed by FIELD_NAME → required value. Field hidden until predicate satisfied. Pass a string for exact match, or an array of strings for any-match (e.g. EMAIL_FROM should show for resend OR postmark OR emailit OR smtp).

hideIf.description: Inverse of showIf. Field is hidden when this predicate matches, regardless of showIf. Used for fields that become irrelevant once another setting is on — e.g. DNS_PROVIDER and its credentials become moot when CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_ENABLED is true (Caddy uses tls-internal then; no ACME challenge runs). Same value semantics as showIf: string for exact match, array for any-match.

postSaveJob.description: Background job triggered after save. e.g. 'corpus-sync' for Tax-Research-Chat ENABLED_STATES.

healthCheckTimeout.description: Override the default 90s post-restart health-check window. Apps with slow warm-up (e.g. LLM-backed) may need 180+.

disabledImpacts.description: Strings naming features that break if this setting is set to a disabling value (e.g. EMAIL_PROVIDER=none disables 'client-portal-in-vibe-connect'). The Settings page surfaces these as a confirmation dialog before save.
